overview: Stonemasons build and repair walls, walkways, fireplaces and building fronts using natural and artificial stone. They lay out patterns and foundations, cut and shape stone, set it in mortar and check alignment with levels and plumb lines. O*NET rates knowledge of building and construction at 4.68 out of 5 for this job and design at 3.68. Most learn as helpers or apprentices; 58% have a high school diploma and 42% less in O*NET data. The BLS May 2025 median is $57,390, in a small trade of 7,820 jobs. The work is heavy, outdoors and on your feet.
pay: Stonemasons earn a median of $57,390, and the top 10% earn $86,180 or more. Wisconsin has the highest state median at $82,740, 44% above the national figure, followed by Nevada and Washington. California has the most stonemasons, 1,250, at a median of $60,930, and Texas has 420.

faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $57,390 a year. The middle half earn between $45,450 and $71,630. Wisconsin, Nevada ($79,600) and Washington ($78,010) have the highest state medians, while Oklahoma ($40,930) and Mississippi ($40,700) pay the least. Restoration specialists often earn more.

faq.q: How do you become a stonemason?
faq.a: Most start as helpers and learn on the job, or join an apprenticeship that lasts about 3 to 4 years. In O*NET data, 58% of stonemasons have a high school diploma and 42% less than one. O*NET places the job in Job Zone 2.

Yes. In O*NET data the job ranks above 99% of U.S. jobs for time on your feet, and long weeks are common. You lift heavy stone, work outdoors in all weather and must place each piece accurately, since mistakes can be costly to fix.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to stonemason?
faq.a: The closest moves are masonry helpers (84% match), manufacturing stone cutters and carvers (81%) and surface mining machine operators (76%), based on O*NET 31.0. Layout Workers are a 75% match and earn $63,870, 11% more, according to BLS May 2025 data.
